title: Building with Purpose
author: acrolicious
selftext:
For nearly 10 years, my brother Ben lived without digital access, communication, or independence.

Ben has an ultra-rare condition that took his ability to walk, talk, and use his hands. Over the years, we hit brick wall after brick wall with mainstream assistive tech. Eye-tracking failed due to low vision and nystagmus. Head-tracking, EMG switches, and EEG systems didn't work because he lacks the fine motor control required to operate them.

For a decade, his world was limited to left and right head movements for "yes" or "no."

No television access. No games. No independent communication.

Then, AI changed everything.

Because of modern AI tools, I've been able to code and build custom, accessible (and engaging) software over the last two years specifically designed around the only two physical buttons Ben can reliably use.

Watching him regain independence, play games, and navigate digital spaces has been nothing short of a dream come true.

Time matters. Today, we can build better, smarter, and faster than ever before—and it is making an immediate, profound difference in Ben's quality of life. I couldn't be more thankful.

My goal in sharing this is simple: to remind people that there are countless individuals out there facing the exact same barriers, sitting in silence with limited options and outdated gear. But today, there is more hope than ever before.

We don't keep what we build behind a paywall. Everything we create is 100% free and open-source:

 \* switchedgames.org: Custom, free accessible web games playable with a single switch.

 \* bennyshub.com: A completely free hub of tools and platforms built for users with specific physical and intellectual access needs.

Every single feature on these platforms is designed to be fully navigable with simple switch inputs, giving individuals with profound physical limitations true independence.

This is why I build.

He isn't able to vocalize on command. All the accessibility information is on GitHub 

https://github.com/NARBEHOUSE/Narbehouse.github.io/tree/main/bennyshub

comments.author: lin_dhu
comments.body:
Not hating or anything, but asking out of pure curiosity.  
Because the post is worded in a way that sounds like this game was impossible to make this without ai, is it because  
1. there's something unique that the generative ai technology offered?  
2. or purely a time issue? Like being able to create an accessible game in short amount of time when other game dev is less interested in making games for such a small audience?

I'm not hating on either reasons btw but I wanted to know if there are specific accessibility tools that only generative ai was able to offer cuz I couldn't get what it is from the post.

replies.author: acrolicious
replies.body:
Not impossible. The issue was that no one built them for Ben's specific needs. And, since his condition is progressive, instead of adapting around the game, the game can adapt to him and exactly how his body and mind can process. This is something you need something to build and iterate on fast. It would have taken months or years and probably tens of thousands of dollars to build an app like this with all the games and features- time and money we don't have. And by the time it would have been completed, we would probably need to modify again.

AI is able to do that, instantly, as Ben's needs change.

replies.author: acrolicious
replies.body:
There's nothing to monetize. AI is moving so fast, this "product" is a message. You can build now using AI for these kinds of things.

Full transparency: We raise money through our nonprofit and have a tips page AND we get a little ad revenue from our social media. 

However, the nonprofit runs lean since we volunteer all of our time (it pays for hosting, some AI credits and the switch kit program). We don't get many tips and we only put it up there for people who want to buy us a cup of coffee. Ad revenue gets re-donated back into our foundation as our own contribution. 

We just want to give Ben a good time, show his perseverance (yes, with his consent- he reviews and approved everything we put online) and help people if we can. It's that simple. 

AI is going to make all of our apps and probably what we are doing pretty trivial in the not so distant future (I hope) so there's no future outside of trying to find more people like Ben and ensuring they aren't left out. That's ultimately the point.

replies.author: acrolicious
replies.body:
It's purely recreational. Going down the road of classifications for what can be a clinical / medical device isn't something we want to explore. We made it open source so if someone wanted to take it there, please do! 

We are just a family showing what's possible and publishing what we made freely so others can get access if they can't build their own right now.
